Older age is historically associated with frailty, multimorbidity, and greater disability burden.
Sex differences may influence body composition, disease patterns, and functional decline.
Race/ethnicity may reflect disparities, access, environment, and population heterogeneity rather than direct biology.
Education is a socioeconomic proxy related to health literacy, prevention, and healthcare utilization.
Income-poverty ratio captures socioeconomic resources that may affect disease burden and function.
BMI summarizes body-size status and is linked to obesity, metabolic disease, frailty, and mobility limitation.
Height is a body-size measure, useful mainly through its contribution to BMI and body composition context.
Weight reflects body mass burden and may influence mobility and metabolic status.
Systolic blood pressure reflects vascular burden and is often linked with aging and chronic disease.
Diastolic blood pressure complements SBP but is often less informative than systolic pressure in older adults.
Grip strength is a recognized marker of frailty, sarcopenia, and functional reserve.
HbA1c reflects chronic glycemic control and long-term metabolic burden.
Fasting glucose reflects current glycemic status and complements HbA1c.
Total cholesterol reflects cardiometabolic burden, though it may not directly map to disability.
HDL is a protective lipid marker and may be inversely related to metabolic risk.
Triglycerides often indicate insulin resistance and cardiometabolic dysfunction.
LDL is clinically relevant but partially derived from other lipid variables, so redundancy is possible.
Smoking reflects a damaging behavioral exposure associated with vascular and systemic disease.
Weekly MET-minutes summarize physical activity and are expected to be protective against disability.
A thresholded summary of activity level, mainly useful for simplified interpretation.
Sedentary behavior captures inactivity burden beyond exercise quantity.
Depression burden may worsen physical function, motivation, and overall disability.
Categorized depression severity simplifies interpretation but may lose detail versus the raw score.
Arthritis is a direct structural disease mechanism affecting pain, function, and disability.
Arthritis subtype may add nuance but is conditional and often sparse.
Medication burden is a practical proxy for multimorbidity and overall clinical complexity.
Binary medication burden summary; useful clinically but less informative than the count.
